limitations: Each scenario/action row is one observation. Different populations, scenes, paths and runtimes are not comparable performance baselines.
Pause is complete before exit is requested in these trials. Zero exit pause-stage time does not mean pausing is free.
Menu response ends after two processed frames, not a display-photodiode measurement.

Save stage measures viewer request through terminal response: confirmed acknowledgement on successful save rows, rejection on the deliberate save_error row. It includes validation, disk work and transport; it is not pure disk-write time.
Window disappearance is not timestamped directly; viewer-exit observation and final-log metadata use launcher timestamps.
Whole application timing includes startup, scripted operations, screenshot capture and 250 ms process polling. Checkpoint reload verification runs afterward.
Existing caches were used. No claim of cold-start speed, FPS improvement or supported population capacity is made.
Final save-error wording was verified after the successful version-2 trials; source hashes are retained per trial.
Raw local reports may contain local paths and synthetic state. Public evidence includes aggregate fields only.
Atomic saves and graceful cleanup cannot guarantee persistence after hardware or operating-system failure.

check_semantics.recovery_valid: Successful save rows: checkpoint reload validated acknowledged tick, roster and paused state. The save_error row: expected failure behavior passed, the blocking directory remained and no recovery was reloaded. This key does not certify a valid checkpoint in a failed-save row.
